content.text:
Yes, eventually. For this site, I’d do RSS now. Add newsletter later, once posting cadence proves itself.

RSS, plain English

RSS means “Really Simple Syndication.” It is a public update URL, usually XML.

Flow:

1. Site publishes `/feed.xml`.
2. Reader copies that URL into Feedly, NetNewsWire, Inoreader, etc.
3. Reader checks URL periodically.
4. New posts appear automatically.

RSS is pull. Reader checks site.

Newsletter is push. Visitor gives email, then your email service sends new-post messages.

RSS:

- no signup
- no email collection
- no unsubscribe system
- reader controls timing
- privacy-friendly
- good for technical readers

Newsletter:

- reaches casual readers directly
- better chance they notice new posts
- needs consent, unsubscribe, email delivery, privacy handling
- creates pressure to send regularly

Your repo already has RSS:

- [`app/feed.xml/route.ts`](/Users/dhruv2mars/dev/github/portfolio/app/feed.xml/route.ts) generates it.
- Published MDX posts enter the feed.
- Drafts stay out.
- Feed contains title, summary, link, date.
- Footer already links to it in [`components/site-footer.tsx`](/Users/dhruv2mars/dev/github/portfolio/components/site-footer.tsx).

Important difference: RSS is not email. It is closer to a bookmark that keeps updating itself.

Best plan:

- Keep RSS as default.
- Add a visible “RSS” link near Blog, not only in footer.
- Add newsletter signup once you can honestly promise useful emails, such as one per substantial post.
- Use same post source for both. Current RSS sends summaries, so automated newsletter emails would also be summaries unless we expand the feed.

Verdict: both can exist. RSS serves committed readers. Newsletter serves everyone else. Newsletter is optional; RSS is the clean foundation.
